title: Part I Protheoria: Threefold later controversy — calumnies, adiaphora, real heads
pass_a_gloss: From that time: Controversies with Flaccians & Bergen men and their grandsons in nearly threefold difference — besides the prior one on Lord's Supper / mode of receiving Christ's Body in Eucharist. I. Controversies not born from Reformers' doctrine but from its extortions — not from things handed down but from affixed things — so not questions of right but of fact. E.g. Do Reformed make natural Reason judge of faith-sentences, or Philosophy principle of Theological conclusions? Assert absolute necessity of human acts, Stoic fate, Manichaean or Predestinarian Heresy? Make God author/cause (physical or moral) of Sin? Deny God's Omnipotence (corporal presence chapter) or Mercy (universal Grace chapter)? Divide Christ's Natures / think with Nestorius because they distinguish Natures in Person-unity? Take away force/efficacy of Christ's Death? Are Sacraments bare signs/tokens to them? Deny/attack all Christ's Eucharistic presence? Deny all grace to Infants, or seed of faith/grace/regeneration, etc.? These Controversies as calumnious are in the matter itself null — yet Eckhard, Meisner, Musaeus, Gerhard, Hutter, Mentzer, Calov, Dorsch, Danhauer, Schlüsselburg, etc. are laborious and almost wholly about them. II. Some less principal/weighty: certain Adiaphorous Rites & Ceremonies around Baptism, Eucharist, Confession, kneeling at Jesus' name, temple adornment, Images, Feasts, etc. — not equally used by all Lutherans; partly born from Luther's temper vs Carlstadt on Images, etc. III. Finally more real/principal Controversies on Doctrine heads arisen after Luther: Person of Christ & Omnipresence of Human Nature; Predestination & annexed; then Baptism. These we chiefly attend here, as also the Eucharistic Controversy, so our Hearers may know the State of the Controversy. See more fully in Ursinus, Polanus, Zanchi, Sadeel, Beza, Danaeus, Pareus, Wendelin, Alting, Masson, J. Crocius, Maresius, Hoornbeek, Hottinger, Arnold, Heidegger, etc.
pass_b_english: From that time there have been Controversies with the Flaccians, and with the Bergen men, and with their grandsons, in nearly a threefold difference — besides that prior one concerning the Lord's Supper, or the mode of receiving Christ's Body in the Eucharist. I. Other Controversies not born from the doctrine of the Reformers, but from extortions of it — not from things handed down, but from things affixed — which are therefore not questions of right, but of fact. For example: Whether the Reformed make natural Reason the Judge of sentences of faith; or Philosophy the principle of Theological conclusions? Whether they assert an absolute necessity of human actions, a Stoic fate, a Manichaean or Predestinarian Heresy? Whether they so make God the author or cause — physical or moral — of Sin? Whether they deny God's Omnipotence, in the Chapter of Corporal presence, or His Mercy, in the other Chapter of Universal Grace? Likewise whether they divide the Natures of Christ, or think with Nestorius, because they distinguish the Natures in the unity of the Person? Whether they take away the force and efficacy of Christ's Death? Whether the Sacraments are to them bare signs, bare tokens? Whether they deny and assail every presence of Christ in the Eucharist? Whether they deny all grace to Infants, or the seed of faith, of grace, of regeneration, and so on? And these Controversies, as they are calumnious, so in the matter itself they are null — about which nevertheless Eckhard, Meisner, Musaeus, Gerhard, Hutter, Mentzer, Calov, Dorsch, Danhauer, Schlüsselburg, and others are laborious and almost wholly occupied.

II. Certain others are less principal or weighty — for example, concerning certain Adiaphorous Rites and Ceremonies around Baptism, the Eucharist, Confession, kneeling at the name of Jesus, or the adornment of Temples, the use of Images, of Feasts, and so on. Which Rites it is agreed are not equally employed by all Lutherans, having arisen partly from Luther's temper against Carolostadius in the cause of Images, and so on. III. Finally other Controversies are more real, or principal, concerning Heads of Doctrine that arose after Luther: for example concerning the Person of Christ, and the Omnipresence of the Human Nature; concerning Predestination and its annexed heads; and at last concerning Baptism. And these we chiefly attend to in this place, as also the Eucharistic Controversy, so that the State of the Controversy may be clear to our Hearers. They are to be seen more fully in Ursinus, Polanus, Zanchi, Sadeel, Beza, Danaeus, Pareus, Wendelin, Alting, Masson, Johann Crocius, Maresius, Hoornbeek, Hottinger, Arnold, Heidegger, and others.
source_text: Ab eo tempore fuerunt Controversiae cum Flaccianis, & Bergensibus, horumque nepotibus, in triplici fere differentia; praeter priorem illam de Coena Domini, seu de modo percipiendi Corporis Christi in Eucharistia. I. Aliae Controversiae non ex doctrina Reformatorum natae, sed extorsionibus illius, non ex traditis, sed ex affictis, quae adeo non juris quaestiones sunt, sed facti. V. gr. An Reformati Rationem naturalem faciant Judicem sententiarum fidei; vel Philosophiam principium conclusionum Theologicarum? An statuant necessitatem absolutam actionum humanarum, fatum Stoicum, Haeresim Manichaeam, vel Praedestinatianam? An Deum adeo faciant auctorem vel causam, seu physicam, seu moralem Peccati? An negent Dei Omnipotentiam, in Cap. praesentiae Corporalis, vel Misericordiam, in altero Gratiae Universalis? Sic an dividant Naturas Christi, aut cum Nestorio sentiant, quia Naturas in unitate Personae distinguunt? An vim & efficaciam Mortis Christi tollant? An Sacramenta sint ipsis nuda signa, nudae tesserae? An praesentiam Christi in Eucharistia omnem negent, oppugnent? An negent gratiam omnem Infantibus, aut semen fidei, gratiae, regenerationis, &c. Et hae Controversiae ut calumniosae, sic re ipsa sunt nullae, circa quas tamen operosi sunt ac fere toti Eckhardus, Meisnerus, Musaeus, Gerhardus, Hutterus, Mentzerus, Calovius, Dorschaus, Danhawerus, Schlüsselburgius, &c. II. Aliae quaedam minus principales aut momentosae sunt, puta, de Ritibus quibusdam & Ceremoniis Adiaphoris, circa Baptismum, Eucharistiam, Confessionem, Genuflexionem ad nomen Jesu, vel ornatum Templorum, usum Imaginum, Festorum, &c. Quos Ritus nec ab omnibus Lutheranis perinde adhiberi constat, ortos partim ex Lutheri in Carolostadium animis, in causa Imaginum, &c. III. Aliae denique Controversiae magis reales sunt, seu principales, de Doctrinae capitibus, quae sunt post Lutherum exorta: Puta de Persona Christi, & Omnipraesentia Naturae Humanae; de Praedestinatione & annexis; tandemque de Baptismo. Et has potissimum hoc in loco attendimus, ut & Controversiam Eucharisticam, quo de Statu Controversiae nostris Auditoribus constet. Videndae plenius apud Ursinum, Polanum, Zanchium, Sadeelem, Bezam, Danaeum, Pareum, Wendelinum, Altingium, Massonium, J. Crocium, Maresium, Hoornbekium, Hottingerum, Arnoldum, Heideggerum, &c.
